q: A fuel is a substance that releases sufficient energy to do work as it undergoes a ____ change.
e: A fuel is a substance that releases sufficient energy to do work as it undergoes a chemical change. A chemical change makes new substances, like burning or cooking rice.

q: Crude oil, coal and natural gas are called ____ fuels because they are formed from the remains of plants and animals that lived millions of years ago.
e: Crude oil, coal and natural gas are called fossil fuels because they are formed from the remains of plants and animals that lived millions of years ago. Fossil fuels are coal, petroleum, and natural gas, formed from ancient remains and finite.

q: These fuels are classified as ____ and are finite (limited) resources because they take a very long time to form.
e: These fuels are classified as non-renewable and are finite (limited) resources because they take a very long time to form. Non-renewable is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are three major fossil fuels: coal, crude oil and ____ gas.
e: There are three major fossil fuels: coal, crude oil and natural gas. Natural is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Coal is fossilised plant material containing mainly carbon together with hydrogen, nitrogen and ____.
e: Coal is fossilised plant material containing mainly carbon together with hydrogen, nitrogen and sulphur. Sulphur is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most coal was formed during the ____ period (286-360 million years ago).
e: Most coal was formed during the Carboniferous period (286-360 million years ago). Carboniferous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The action of pressure and heat through geological forces converted the plant material in stages from peat to lignite to bituminous soft coal to hard coal (____).
e: The action of pressure and heat through geological forces converted the plant material in stages from peat to lignite to bituminous soft coal to hard coal (anthracite). Anthracite is the idea that completes this fact.

q: At each stage of coal formation, the percentage of ____ increases.
e: At each stage of coal formation, the percentage of carbon increases. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: Coal contains between 80 to ____% carbon by mass.
e: Coal contains between 80 to 90% carbon by mass. 90 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: MYANMAR also has coal deposits in Shan State, Kachin State, Taninthayi Region and ____ Region.
e: MYANMAR also has coal deposits in Shan State, Kachin State, Taninthayi Region and Sagaing Region. Sagaing is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When coal is burnt, the main products are carbon dioxide and ____.
e: When coal is burnt, the main products are carbon dioxide and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When coal is strongly heated in the absence of air a solid called ____ is produced.
e: When coal is strongly heated in the absence of air a solid called coke is produced. Coke is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The main use of coke is as a ____ agent in the blast furnace for making iron.
e: The main use of coke is as a reducing agent in the blast furnace for making iron. Reducing is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Crude oil (also called ____) is a thick black liquid.
e: Crude oil (also called petroleum) is a thick black liquid. Petroleum is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Today, about ____% of the world's energy comes from petroleum while 20% comes from natural gas.
e: Today, about 40% of the world's energy comes from petroleum while 20% comes from natural gas. 40 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: British Burma exported its first barrel of crude oil in ____.
e: British Burma exported its first barrel of crude oil in 1853. 1853 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The London-based Burma Oil Company (BOC) began production in the ____ oil field in 1887.
e: The London-based Burma Oil Company (BOC) began production in the Yenangyaung oil field in 1887. Yenangyaung is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The crude oil and natural gas were formed from dead animals and plants that lived in the ____ a long time ago.
e: The crude oil and natural gas were formed from dead animals and plants that lived in the seas a long time ago. Seas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: High pressure and temperature changed it into petroleum over millions of ____.
e: High pressure and temperature changed it into petroleum over millions of years. Years is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrocarbons are made up of hydrogen and ____ only.
e: Hydrocarbons are made up of hydrogen and carbon only. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit. A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon.

q: Natural gas consists mainly of methane (85-95%) with varying amounts of ethane, propane, butane and other gases such as carbon dioxide, nitrogen, hydrogen ____, etc.
e: Natural gas consists mainly of methane (85-95%) with varying amounts of ethane, propane, butane and other gases such as carbon dioxide, nitrogen, hydrogen sulphide, etc. Sulphide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The fuels that are derived from petroleum support more than ____ of the world's total energy production.
e: The fuels that are derived from petroleum support more than half of the world's total energy production. Half is the idea that completes this fact.

q: As of 2015, Myanmar exports gas to Thailand and ____.
e: As of 2015, Myanmar exports gas to Thailand and China. China is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Natural gas consists mainly of methane, ____.
e: Natural gas consists mainly of methane, CH4. CH4 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Crude oil is a mixture of many different ____ molecules.
e: Crude oil is a mixture of many different hydrocarbon molecules. A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon.

q: The small molecules have few carbon atoms and ____ boiling points, while the large molecules have many carbon atoms and high boiling points.
e: The small molecules have few carbon atoms and low boiling points, while the large molecules have many carbon atoms and high boiling points. Low is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Separation of the crude oil takes place in a fractional distillation column, or ____ tower, into different fractions in an oil refinery.
e: Separation of the crude oil takes place in a fractional distillation column, or fractionating tower, into different fractions in an oil refinery. A fractionating column lets a liquid mixture split into fractions with different boiling points.

q: The oil ____ and passes up the fractionating column.
e: The oil vaporises and passes up the fractionating column. Vaporises is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The fractions condense and come out of the column at different heights depending on their ____ points.
e: The fractions condense and come out of the column at different heights depending on their boiling points. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

q: The petroleum gas fraction comes out first at the top of the column as its molecules have the ____ boiling points.
e: The petroleum gas fraction comes out first at the top of the column as its molecules have the lowest boiling points. Lowest is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A series of fractions such as petrol, naphtha, kerosene and diesel comes out in order of increasing boiling points, number of carbon atoms and ____.
e: A series of fractions such as petrol, naphtha, kerosene and diesel comes out in order of increasing boiling points, number of carbon atoms and viscosity. Viscosity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bitumen is the ____ at the bottom of the column.
e: Bitumen is the residue at the bottom of the column. Residue is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All the fractions are insoluble in ____ and burn in air.
e: All the fractions are insoluble in water and burn in air. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Refinery gas has approximately 1 to ____ carbon atoms per molecule.
e: Refinery gas has approximately 1 to 4 carbon atoms per molecule. 4 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Refinery gas has a boiling point range of below room temperature, specifically less than ____°C.
e: Refinery gas has a boiling point range of below room temperature, specifically less than 40°C. 40 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Petrol has approximately 5 to ____ carbon atoms per molecule.
e: Petrol has approximately 5 to 10 carbon atoms per molecule. 10 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Petrol has a boiling point range of ____ to 75°C.
e: Petrol has a boiling point range of 35 to 75°C. 35 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Naphtha is used to make ____.
e: Naphtha is used to make petrochemicals. Petrochemicals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Paraffin (kerosene) has a boiling point range of 170 to ____°C.
e: Paraffin (kerosene) has a boiling point range of 170 to 250°C. 250 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Paraffin has approximately 10 to ____ carbon atoms per molecule.
e: Paraffin has approximately 10 to 14 carbon atoms per molecule. 14 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Diesel oil is used as fuel for diesel engines of buses, lorries, trucks, steamers and ____.
e: Diesel oil is used as fuel for diesel engines of buses, lorries, trucks, steamers and trains. Trains is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Diesel oil has approximately 15 to ____ carbon atoms per molecule.
e: Diesel oil has approximately 15 to 25 carbon atoms per molecule. 25 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lubricating oil has a boiling point range of 350 to ____°C.
e: Lubricating oil has a boiling point range of 350 to 500°C. 500 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lubricating oil is used as a lubricant in engines to reduce ____.
e: Lubricating oil is used as a lubricant in engines to reduce friction. Friction is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fuel oil has a boiling point range of 500 to ____°C.
e: Fuel oil has a boiling point range of 500 to 600°C. 600 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bitumen is a black substance used to make surface roads and ____.
e: Bitumen is a black substance used to make surface roads and roofing. Roofing is the idea that completes this fact.

q: 'Crude oil' (UK) is the same as '____' (USA).
e: 'Crude oil' (UK) is the same as 'petroleum' (USA). Petroleum is the idea that completes this fact.

q: 'Petrol' (UK) is the same as '____' (USA).
e: 'Petrol' (UK) is the same as 'gasoline' (USA). Gasoline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: 'Paraffin' (UK) is the same as '____' (USA).
e: 'Paraffin' (UK) is the same as 'kerosene' (USA). Kerosene is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There is a greater demand for petrol and ____ than other fractions.
e: There is a greater demand for petrol and kerosene than other fractions. Kerosene is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cracking is a thermal decomposition process in which large alkane hydrocarbon molecules are broken down by passing them over a heated ____ under pressure.
e: Cracking is a thermal decomposition process in which large alkane hydrocarbon molecules are broken down by passing them over a heated catalyst under pressure. Catalyst is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The products are smaller alkanes used for fuels and ____ which are used to make polymers.
e: The products are smaller alkanes used for fuels and alkenes which are used to make polymers. Alkenes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In this reactor, particles of catalyst are mixed with the hydrocarbon fraction at a temperature around ____°C and moderately low pressure.
e: In this reactor, particles of catalyst are mixed with the hydrocarbon fraction at a temperature around 500°C and moderately low pressure. 500 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The catalyst is made of powdered minerals such as silica, alumina and ____.
e: The catalyst is made of powdered minerals such as silica, alumina and zeolites. Zeolites is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cracking reactions generally give two main types of products: an alkane with a shorter chain than the original and a short-chain ____ molecule.
e: Cracking reactions generally give two main types of products: an alkane with a shorter chain than the original and a short-chain alkene molecule. Alkene is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shortened alkanes can be blended with the gasoline fraction to enrich the ____.
e: The shortened alkanes can be blended with the gasoline fraction to enrich the petrol. Petrol is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ethene polymerises to ____.
e: Ethene polymerises to polyethene. Polyethene is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Propene polymerises to polypropene, while butene polymerises to produce synthetic ____.
e: Propene polymerises to polypropene, while butene polymerises to produce synthetic rubber. Rubber is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The alkane produced from cracking may turn to a branched isomer on heating with the catalyst, giving it a higher ____ rating.
e: The alkane produced from cracking may turn to a branched isomer on heating with the catalyst, giving it a higher octane rating. Octane rating tells how well a petrol resists knocking in an engine.

q: The higher the octane number, the greater the fuel's resistance to ____ in an internal combustion engine.
e: The higher the octane number, the greater the fuel's resistance to knocking in an internal combustion engine. Octane rating tells how well a petrol resists knocking in an engine.

q: The octane number of a given fuel is determined by comparing it with two standard reference fuels: iso-octane and ____.
e: The octane number of a given fuel is determined by comparing it with two standard reference fuels: iso-octane and heptane. Heptane is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iso-octane resists knocking and has an octane number of ____.
e: Iso-octane resists knocking and has an octane number of 100. 100 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Heptane causes knocking and has an octane number of ____.
e: Heptane causes knocking and has an octane number of 0. 0 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An antiknocking agent, such as ____, is a gasoline additive used to reduce engine knocking.
e: An antiknocking agent, such as tetraethyl lead, is a gasoline additive used to reduce engine knocking. Tetraethyl lead is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A catalyst is a substance that speeds up the chemical reaction without getting ____.
e: A catalyst is a substance that speeds up the chemical reaction without getting consumed. Consumed is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Zeolites are microporous, aluminosilicate minerals commonly used as commercial adsorbents and ____.
e: Zeolites are microporous, aluminosilicate minerals commonly used as commercial adsorbents and catalysts. Catalysts is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thermal decomposition is the breaking down of a chemical compound, caused by ____.
e: Thermal decomposition is the breaking down of a chemical compound, caused by heat. Heat is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Engine knocking refers to the sharp sounds caused by combustion of some of the compressed ____ mixture in the cylinder.
e: Engine knocking refers to the sharp sounds caused by combustion of some of the compressed air-fuel mixture in the cylinder. A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy as it changes chemically, usually by burning.

q: At the present rate of consumption, petroleum and natural gas may run out within ____ years.
e: At the present rate of consumption, petroleum and natural gas may run out within 50 years. 50 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: At the present rate of consumption, coal will only last for a further ____ years.
e: At the present rate of consumption, coal will only last for a further 250 years. 250 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An alternative fuel is an internal combustion engine fuel other than gasoline or ____ oil.
e: An alternative fuel is an internal combustion engine fuel other than gasoline or diesel oil. Diesel is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Alternative fuels include natural gas, propane, hydrogen fuel, biomass-derived fuels, biodiesel, bio-alcohols and ____.
e: Alternative fuels include natural gas, propane, hydrogen fuel, biomass-derived fuels, biodiesel, bio-alcohols and electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrogen fuel, biomass-derived fuels, biodiesel and bio-alcohols are ____ fuels.
e: Hydrogen fuel, biomass-derived fuels, biodiesel and bio-alcohols are renewable fuels. Renewable is the idea that completes this fact.

q: LPG stands for Liquefied ____ Gas.
e: LPG stands for Liquefied Petroleum Gas. Petroleum is the idea that completes this fact.

q: LPG is composed of propane and ____.
e: LPG is composed of propane and butane. Butane is the idea that completes this fact.

q: CNG contains 90% ____.
e: CNG contains 90% methane. Methane is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biodiesel is composed of long chain ____.
e: Biodiesel is composed of long chain esters. Esters is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biogas is produced from waste organic matter and its main composition is ____.
e: Biogas is produced from waste organic matter and its main composition is methane. Methane is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Gasohol is a blended fuel of petrol and ____.
e: Gasohol is a blended fuel of petrol and ethanol. Ethanol is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A common gasohol mixture is 90% petrol and ____% ethanol.
e: A common gasohol mixture is 90% petrol and 10% ethanol. 10 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plant or animal oils have to be converted to biodiesel by ____.
e: Plant or animal oils have to be converted to biodiesel by Transesterification. Transesterification is used to make biodiesel from oils and an alcohol.

q: The transesterification process involves the addition of potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide as a basic ____.
e: The transesterification process involves the addition of potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide as a basic catalyst. Catalyst is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The solution is heated to ____°C during the transesterification process.
e: The solution is heated to 60°C during the transesterification process. 60 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The transesterification process produces methyl or ethyl ester as the product and ____.
e: The transesterification process produces methyl or ethyl ester as the product and glycerol. Glycerol is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pure biodiesel is separated out by removing glycerine and sodium or potassium salt of fatty acids, which is also known as ____.
e: Pure biodiesel is separated out by removing glycerine and sodium or potassium salt of fatty acids, which is also known as soap. Turning fat into soap is an old chemical change, a kind of saponification.

q: Most hydrogen is manufactured on a large scale in industry from petrol and natural ____.
e: Most hydrogen is manufactured on a large scale in industry from petrol and natural gas. Gas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A mixture of methane and steam is passed over a ____ catalyst to produce carbon monoxide and hydrogen.
e: A mixture of methane and steam is passed over a nickel catalyst to produce carbon monoxide and hydrogen. Nickel is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The carbon monoxide gas is then reacted with more steam to produce carbon dioxide and ____.
e: The carbon monoxide gas is then reacted with more steam to produce carbon dioxide and hydrogen. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: The hydrogen is separated from the carbon dioxide by passing the gases through an ____ to absorb the acidic carbon dioxide.
e: The hydrogen is separated from the carbon dioxide by passing the gases through an alkali to absorb the acidic carbon dioxide. An alkali is a soluble base that produces OH- ions in water.

q: Smaller quantities of hydrogen are produced by the electrolysis of water containing ____ acid.
e: Smaller quantities of hydrogen are produced by the electrolysis of water containing sulphuric acid. Sulphuric is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The chemical equation for the electrolysis of water is $2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2(g) +$ ____.
e: The chemical equation for the electrolysis of water is 2H2O(l) to 2H2(g) + O2(g). O2(g) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrogen burns cleanly in air, and the product is ____, which is a non-pollutant.
e: Hydrogen burns cleanly in air, and the product is steam, which is a non-pollutant. Steam is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The chemical equation for hydrogen burning in air is $2H_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow$ ____.
e: The chemical equation for hydrogen burning in air is 2H2(g) + O2(g) to 2H2O(g). 2H2O(g) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrogen produces at least twice as much heat energy per gram when burnt, than any other common ____.
e: Hydrogen produces at least twice as much heat energy per gram when burnt, than any other common fuel. A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy as it changes chemically, usually by burning.

q: Methane gas is formed naturally when anaerobic bacteria help decomposition of organic matter under geological conditions to produce natural ____.
e: Methane gas is formed naturally when anaerobic bacteria help decomposition of organic matter under geological conditions to produce natural gas. Gas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In India and China, biomass ____ are important sources of fuel for villages.
e: In India and China, biomass digesters are important sources of fuel for villages. Digesters is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The order for the main energy sources currently used in the world in terms of producing energy is: crude oil > coal > natural gas > hydroelectric > nuclear fission > wind > biofuels > solar > ____.
e: The order for the main energy sources currently used in the world in terms of producing energy is: crude oil > coal > natural gas > hydroelectric > nuclear fission > wind > biofuels > solar > geothermal. Geothermal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plant oil, hydroelectric, wind, biofuels, solar and geothermal are all ____ energy sources.
e: Plant oil, hydroelectric, wind, biofuels, solar and geothermal are all renewable energy sources. Renewable is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Natural gas offshore projects in Myanmar are Yadana project, Yetagon project, Shwe Platform project and ____ project.
e: Natural gas offshore projects in Myanmar are Yadana project, Yetagon project, Shwe Platform project and Zawtika project. Zawtika is the idea that completes this fact.
